evals.prompt: I'm building a new microservice for managing customer data. The service name is 'customer-service', base package is 'com.mycompany.customer', and I want it to run on port 8081. Create the full Spring Boot project scaffold following best practices.
evals.expected_output: Complete Spring Boot project structure with: pom.xml configured for Spring Boot 4.0.3 with PostgreSQL, Lombok, Eureka, SpringDoc OpenAPI; application.yml with server port 8081, database config, Eureka settings; GlobalExceptionHandler with @RestControllerAdvice; ErrorResponse DTO; sample Request/Response DTO templates; Repository, Service, and Controller base classes with proper annotations; all following 3-tier layered architecture pattern

evals.prompt: Create a Spring Boot project for an 'order-processor' service with package 'io.github.ecommerce.order' running on port 8082. The service will handle order processing and payment tracking.
evals.expected_output: Fully scaffolded Spring Boot project with: Maven structure matching convention; pom.xml with all required dependencies (Spring Boot 4.0.3, PostgreSQL driver, JPA, Eureka, Swagger); application.yml with port 8082, database connection pool config, Eureka integration; Exception handlers for order-specific errors; DTO templates with validation annotations; Service layer with maptoResponse() pattern; Controller with CRUD endpoints; Repository interface; all code using constructor injection via @RequiredArgsConstructor and Lombok
